definition: A period when a service or system is unavailable.
business_context_example: The outage lasted 40 minutes and affected every user in Europe.

definition: The percentage of time a system is working and available.
business_context_example: We promise 99.9% uptime, which allows about 43 minutes down per month.

definition: A computer that provides data or services to other computers.
business_context_example: The server ran out of disk space at two in the morning.

definition: The delay between a request and a response.
business_context_example: Latency doubled after the update, and users noticed immediately.

definition: The amount of work a system is handling.
business_context_example: The site handles normal load fine; Black Friday is the question.

definition: Stored data kept ready so it loads faster next time.
business_context_example: Clear the cache and try again before you raise a ticket.

definition: To restart a computer or system.
business_context_example: A reboot fixed it, which is annoying but true.

definition: When a program or system stops working suddenly.
business_context_example: The app crashes every time you open two large files.

definition: When a program stops responding but doesn't close.
business_context_example: The screen froze on the payment page, which is the worst place.

definition: An error in software that makes it behave incorrectly.
business_context_example: The bug only appears when the date is the last day of the month.

definition: To make an error happen again on purpose so it can be studied.
business_context_example: We couldn't reproduce the bug until the user sent a screenshot.

definition: To find and remove errors from software.
business_context_example: He spent two hours debugging a problem caused by one missing comma.

definition: A file recording what a system did and when.
business_context_example: The log file showed 400 failed logins from one address.

definition: Text shown when something goes wrong.
business_context_example: Send me the exact error message, not a description of it.

definition: A small update that fixes a problem in software.
business_context_example: The security patch goes out tonight, after business hours.

definition: An urgent fix released outside the normal schedule.
business_context_example: We shipped a hotfix within two hours of the report.

definition: To put new code onto a live system.
business_context_example: Never deploy on a Friday afternoon. Somebody always learns this the hard way.
translation_bg: да пусна код в реална среда

definition: To return a system to a previous working version.
business_context_example: We rolled back the release after eleven minutes.

definition: To make something available gradually to users.
business_context_example: The feature rolls out to 10% of users first.

definition: A document describing what changed in a new version.
business_context_example: Nobody reads release notes until something breaks.

definition: A copy of the live system used for final testing.
business_context_example: It worked in staging, which is the most famous sentence in this industry.

definition: The live system that real users are using.
business_context_example: Never test in production, and never say you have.

definition: A system that tracks changes to code over time.
business_context_example: Version control means you can always see who changed what, and when.

definition: The place where a project's code is stored.
business_context_example: Clone the repository and read the setup file first.

definition: To save a set of changes to the code history.
business_context_example: Small commits with clear messages save hours later.

definition: To combine one set of code changes into another.
business_context_example: Merge it after the review, not before.

definition: Colleagues checking each other's code before it goes live.
business_context_example: Code review caught a mistake that tests didn't.

definition: The parts of a system users don't see, like servers and databases.
business_context_example: The problem is in the back end, so the design won't fix it.

definition: The part of a system users see and interact with.
business_context_example: The front end looks finished, but nothing is connected yet.

definition: A defined way for two systems to talk to each other.
business_context_example: Their API returns the data in a format we have to convert.

definition: Connecting two systems so they work together.
business_context_example: The integration with the payment provider took three weeks.

definition: An organised store of information a system can search.
business_context_example: The database has 400,000 records and no index on that column.

definition: A request for specific information from a database.
business_context_example: That query takes 12 seconds, which is 11 too many.

definition: To make a copy of data in case the original is lost.
business_context_example: We back up nightly and test the restore every quarter.

definition: To bring back data from a backup.
business_context_example: A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a backup.

definition: To move data or systems from one place to another.
business_context_example: We migrate the old records this weekend, when nobody is working.

definition: An old system still in use because replacing it is difficult.
business_context_example: The legacy system runs payroll and nobody dares touch it.

definition: The username and password used to access a system.
business_context_example: Never send credentials by email, even internally.

definition: Security requiring a password plus a second proof of identity.
business_context_example: Two-factor authentication is now mandatory for every account.

definition: The rights a user has to see or change things.
business_context_example: She had read permissions but not write, which caused the confusion.

definition: Full control over a system's settings.
business_context_example: Only two people have admin rights, and that's on purpose.

definition: Fake messages designed to steal passwords or money.
business_context_example: The phishing email copied our invoice template exactly.

definition: Harmful software designed to damage or steal.
business_context_example: The malware arrived in a file called 'invoice_final.pdf.exe'.

definition: An incident where private data is accessed or stolen.
business_context_example: A data breach must be reported within 72 hours.

definition: Coding data so only authorised people can read it.
business_context_example: Encryption in transit and at rest, both, not one.

definition: A system that blocks unwanted network traffic.
business_context_example: The firewall was blocking the new tool's port.

definition: Computing services delivered over the internet.
business_context_example: We moved to the cloud and stopped worrying about hardware.

definition: Software running on the company's own computers, not the cloud.
business_context_example: The bank insists on an on-premise installation.

definition: To formally report a problem to the support system.
business_context_example: Raise a ticket so it doesn't get lost in a chat message.

definition: A problem the team already knows about.
business_context_example: That's a known issue, and the fix is planned for next week.
